notes.meaning: Solomon calls his listeners his children and asks them to welcome a father's correction. He speaks with loving authority to help them gain true understanding. Listening carefully to godly instruction is the first step toward living wisely.

The teacher assures his hearers that his instruction is reliable and good for their souls. His guidance is built on God's truth, so his students must never abandon it. Heeding sound direction helps a person navigate life's hardest troubles successfully.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Early church writer Hippolytus taught that God's law is a good gift, and that a person abandons this law whenever they disobey it.

notes.meaning: Solomon looks back on his own childhood under his father David and his mother Bathsheba. He was tenderly loved and given special care as God's chosen successor. Both of his parents took an active part in shaping his heart and mind.

David urged young Solomon to hold his teachings tightly inside his heart. True obedience requires more than hearing words; it must be stored within and practiced. Godly parents reflect God Himself as they point their children toward true life.

Wisdom and understanding are described as treasures that must be sought out and acquired at any cost. A person needs to make a firm decision to hold on to these teachings and never turn away. In Scripture, to forget God's words means failing to put them into practice.

Wisdom is pictured here as a faithful guardian and companion. If a person loves wisdom and stays close to her, she will keep them safe from harm. Loving what is good protects a believer from making destructive choices.

Wisdom is the most important thing anyone can ever seek. Even if it costs everything you own, obtaining spiritual understanding must come first. God's truth should take priority over every worldly gain if life is to truly prosper.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Following Augustine, Catholic tradition notes that the first step toward wisdom is simply desiring it, calling it the one thing necessary for the soul.

notes.meaning: Holding wisdom in high regard brings real honor back to the student. Embracing her godly guidance lifts a person above a life of foolishness and shame. When we honor God's truth, He exalts our character and our standing.

Wisdom rewards those who love her by placing a graceful garland upon their head. Like the crown given to a victor, this gift represents dignity, beauty, and protection. Walking in God's path clothes a person with honorable character.

The teacher pleads with his child to welcome these truths so that his life may be long and full. Living sensibly and with self-control protects a person's health from reckless, dangerous habits. Following God's path gives the best foundation for a long, blessed life.

A faithful teacher guides his student along well-marked paths that have proved safe for generations. These straight paths keep a person from getting lost in dishonest or crooked living. Walking in wisdom means following God's clear directions for everyday life.

Walking in wisdom gives a person a broad, open space to move without getting trapped. Even when life demands quick action and running, the wise traveler will not trip over hidden traps. An honest life keeps our daily steps free, clear, and secure.

A student must seize godly instruction with a firm grip and never let it go. Holding on to truth requires real effort because our very life depends upon it. Guarding God's wisdom keeps our souls from falling into fatal traps.

The father gives a sharp warning never to take even the first step onto the road of evil people. Joining in the habits and company of wrongdoers pulls a person toward spiritual ruin. Staying entirely off their path is the only safe choice.

The teacher uses rapid commands to tell the young traveler to turn away and keep running. You should not even approach the edge of evil or test out dangerous temptations. Believers must keep the greatest possible distance from sin and all of its invitations.

Sinners can become so devoted to evil that they cannot rest until they cause trouble. Practicing wickedness has become like a second nature and an addiction to them. They lose their sleep unless they can make someone else stumble and fall into ruin.

Cruel people feed on violence and wickedness just like their daily bread and wine. Sin has become their nourishment, and they take pleasure in oppressing others. Their whole life is sustained by unlawful and destructive gains.

The life of an upright person is like the rising morning sun. It begins like the faint light of dawn and shines brighter and brighter until the full noon of day. God's people continually grow in knowledge, grace, and joy until they reach glory.

The road of the wicked is wrapped in thick, pitch-black darkness. Because they turn away from God's light, they constantly stumble without even knowing what caused their fall. Their rebellion against truth leads only to blindness and sudden disaster.

The father calls for wholehearted attention to his sayings. A wise student bows the ear and listens with deep care instead of letting the mind drift. Paying close attention to God's instruction shows that a person is ready to receive His truth.

God's words should never slip out of sight, but must stay continually before our eyes. More than just reading them, we are called to hide them deep within our inner being. Storing God's truth in the center of our desires guides every choice we make.

Those who grasp God's wise instruction find true spiritual vitality for their souls. Obeying godly counsel also preserves physical health by guarding the body from reckless living and destructive passions. God's wisdom brings healing, peace, and wholeness to the entire person.

A person must guard the inner heart above everything else in life. In Scripture, the heart represents the center of our thoughts, affections, and decisions. Whatever fills the heart will eventually flow out into our words, actions, and entire life story.

A believer must throw away dishonest talk, harsh arguments, and deceitful speech. Words come straight from the heart, so twisted speech reveals a corrupted soul. Keeping our lips clean from lies is a necessary step in guarding our walk with God.

Our eyes should look straight ahead with an honest and direct aim. Staring straight forward keeps a traveler from being lured aside by tempting sights on either side of the road. Fixing our minds on God's path protects our steps from sudden trouble.

We are told to weigh our actions carefully before we take a step. Comparing our daily choices against God's Word smooths out the path and removes dangerous obstacles. Careful, obedient planning keeps our journey firm, steady, and secure.

A wise traveler refuses to wander to the right or to the left of God's road. Any detour away from God's commands leads directly toward wickedness and loss. Staying in the center of God's will requires steady, daily discipline of our feet.
